quote: Giebt es unendlich viele Lösungen? Specieller Fall $p-q=2$. oder $p-q=2r$ wo $p, q, r$ Primzahlen sind
english: Are there infinitely many solutions? Special case p−q=2, or p−q=2r where p, q, r are primes.
topic: Notes on solving linear Diophantine equations in primes (including twin primes), a plan to treat this via Weierstrass's theory of elementary factors and the Riemann–Roch theorem, primes among the values of a polynomial, remarks on the nature of mathematics, and a sketch of a proof of the fundamental theorem of algebra.

triage.modern_statement: Hilbert asks whether a linear Diophantine equation in primes has infinitely many solutions. (1) Special case p − q = 2: are there infinitely many pairs of primes that differ by 2? This is the twin prime conjecture. (2) Variant p − q = 2r with p, q and r all prime: are there infinitely many prime triples satisfying it, i.e. p = q + 2r? This is a single linear equation in three prime variables.
triage.answered_by: Case p − q = 2 (twin primes): never answered. Hilbert put it in his 1900 list as part of Problem 8, and it is still open. The strongest partial result is Yitang Zhang's bounded-gaps theorem, submitted to the Annals of Mathematics in April 2013 and published in vol. 179 (2014): infinitely many pairs of primes differ by less than 70 million. Maynard's refined GPY sieve improved this bound. Case p − q = 2r: the sources I retrieved say nothing specific about this equation. Treating one linear equation in three primes is standard circle-method territory (Vinogradov's three-primes method, used by Hua and others from 1938), and Green–Tao's 'Linear equations in primes' (Annals 2010) gives asymptotic counts for general linear systems in primes. I believe those methods settle this case, but I did not find a source that states it directly.

evidence.claim: Hilbert's eighth problem (1900) includes the solvability of two-variable linear Diophantine equations in primes. The twin prime conjecture and the Goldbach conjecture are special cases.
Zhang submitted a paper to the Annals in late April 2013 proving that infinitely many pairs of primes differ by less than 70 million; this is not yet the twin prime conjecture.
Zhang, 'Bounded gaps between primes', Annals of Mathematics 179 (2014), 1121–1174. Maynard's refined GPY sieve followed.
Hua and others applied Vinogradov's circle method to three-prime problems starting in 1938.
Green and Tao, 'Linear equations in primes' (Annals 2010), count solutions in a given range to systems of linear equations whose unknowns are all required to be prime.
Hilbert's 8th problem, including the twin prime conjecture, is still described as profound and unsolved.

triage.why: The twin-prime case is exactly the kind of question Hilbert later published as part of Problem 8 (1900). It is still open, and bounded-gaps work since Zhang (2013) and Maynard–Tao keeps it very active. The p − q = 2r variant is a three-variable linear equation in primes. Circle-method and Green–Tao techniques plausibly settle it, but none of the sources I found states that explicitly. So my high confidence covers the main twin-prime identification, not a definite claim about the variant.
